## About

The *EarthCODE Hackathon* aims to demonstrate how the
[EarthCODE](https://earthcode.esa.int/) project can support the publication of
data coming from different scientific communities to achieve their data needs.
The main objective is to build thematic analysis-ready *"data collections"* for
each Science Cluster
([Polar](https://eo4society.esa.int/communities/scientists/esa-polar-science-cluster/),
[Ocean](https://eo4society.esa.int/communities/scientists/esa-ocean-science-cluster/),
and
[Carbon](https://eo4society.esa.int/communities/scientists/esa-carbon-science-cluster/)),
demonstrating their value in addressing emerging scientific questions. These
collections will integrate a wide range of geophysical variables from different
scientific project outputs and will be delivered in cloud‑optimised formats in
the ESA [Open Science Catalogue](https://opensciencedata.esa.int/). The
intention is to ensure that the scientific community can easily access and use
these data collections to develop new applications, fill existing knowledge
gaps, and explore new research opportunities.

The event will not only highlight the creation of high‑impact data collections
that can be published on EarthCODE and **openly accessed** by anyone but also
will **improve visibility and promote wider uptake of these data sets** across
the scientific community.

The goals of the hackathon are to:

1) **REUSE:** Work with existing EarthCODE thematic data collections and
   services to address scientific questions defined by participating teams.
2) **PUBLISH:** Create new data collections in the [Open Science
   Catalogue](https://opensciencedata.esa.int/) or bring additional data to
   existing collections by using EarthCODE libraries and tools.
3) **LEARN** and implement [FAIR
   principles](https://www.go-fair.org/fair-principles/) for Open Science.
4) **BUILD COMMUNITY:** Build a community around the EarthCODE project and
   datasets in the Open Science Catalogue, fostering collaboration and promoting
   knowledge exchange and the development of new ideas.
5) **CONTRIBUTE:** Propose improvements or extensions to existing EarthCODE
   tools.

Hackathons are participant-driven events that strive to create welcoming spaces
for participants to learn new things, build community and gain hands-on
experience with collaboration and team science. During EarthCODE Hackathon 2026,
we will have a combination of science lectures and coding tutorials and group
projects (pitched by participants).
:::
